Class RcxBrick

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.remote.lego.rcx.RcxBrick
public final class RcxBrick extends Object
The RCX's direct commands that answer back, the protocol under RemoteRcx's motors, sensors, display, sound and battery (as LeJOS builds RemoteNXT on NXTCommand); use RemoteRcx in a program. Set up the link with RemoteRcx.begin() or RcxLink.begin(InfraredReceiver, InfraredEmitter) first, with both the IR LED and the IR receiver module wired. Plain Java on Infrared.

Each call is a request and a reply, which takes 100 ms or more; they return -1 when the brick does not answer (out of range, off, or the IR LED not pointing at it). The opcode and argument encodings have not been verified on a brick.

    • drive

      public void drive(int outputs, int speed)
      Runs the outputs at speed, -7..7: the sign is the direction, the size the power level, and 0 brakes them. That is up to four commands, each waiting for the brick's acknowledgement when the receiver is wired, so one call takes a few hundred milliseconds; set the speed once and not in a tight loop.

    • batteryMillivolts

      public int batteryMillivolts()
      The brick's battery voltage in millivolts (about 9000 with fresh batteries, and the brick warns below about 6000), or -1 if it did not answer. It is a request and a reply, like the sensor reads.

    • playSound

      public boolean playSound(int sound)
      Plays one of the six built-in sounds, RcxAudio.SOUND_*. Returns whether the brick acknowledged the command, which needs the IR receiver wired; the sound then plays on the brick's own speaker and the call returns without waiting for it to end.

    • showNumber

      public boolean showNumber(int value)
      Shows value, limited to RcxLcd.MIN_NUMBER..RcxLcd.MAX_NUMBER, on the brick's display in place of JUno, until the next call. Needs Juno's own RCX firmware (RcxRemoteFirmware); LEGO's firmware does not know the command and does not answer. Returns whether the brick acknowledged.

    • clearDisplay

      public boolean clearDisplay()
      Blanks the display, its number and icons too (but for the IR cones), until a number or text is shown. Needs Juno's own RCX firmware (RcxRemoteFirmware); LEGO's firmware does not answer. Returns whether the brick acknowledged.

    • showText

      public boolean showText(String text)
      Shows the first four characters of text on the display's four digits, left to right, blank past its end, as a seven-segment display draws them (letters such as V, W and M are approximated, and characters it cannot draw show blank). Sends one command per digit; needs Juno's own RCX firmware. Returns whether the brick acknowledged every one.

    • showIcon

      public boolean showIcon(int icon, boolean lit)
      Lights the display icon icon, RcxLcd.ICON_*, or with lit false hands it back to the brick, which lights some icons from its own state: running motors' arrows, pressed touch sensors, low battery, and the minifigure, standing and walking while a motor runs. Needs Juno's own RCX firmware (RcxRemoteFirmware); LEGO's firmware does not know the command and does not answer. Returns whether the brick acknowledged.

    • playTone

      public boolean playTone(int frequencyHz, int durationCentiseconds)
      Plays a tone of frequencyHz (about 31 to 20000 Hz) for durationCentiseconds hundredths of a second (1..255, so up to 2.55 s), then returns without waiting for it to end. Returns whether the brick acknowledged the command. A tone replaces any sound still playing, so wait for the duration before sending the next.

    • clickedButtons

      public int clickedButtons()
      The brick's own buttons clicked since the previous call, Run 0x01, View 0x02, Prgm 0x04, or -1 if no reply. Polls Juno's own source 96, which only Juno's RCX firmware answers.

    • isPressed

      public boolean isPressed(int input)
      Whether the touch sensor on input is pressed; false also when the brick did not answer.
